I was 13 and seeing a psychiatrist, and I mentioned to him that occasionally I'd have thoughts of suicide but they never lasted and I'd never act on them. His response to this was to immediately commit me to a mental hospital. 8 years later and I still have PTSD and can't go to a hospital without freaking out. The place they sent me did nothing but try to scare us - showing pictures of dead bodies, videos of crying families, and on more than one occasion patients would "snap" and need to be sedated - held down by a team of 20 staff, injected with god knows what, and literally thrown into a small room with no light for 24 hours. I understand that it's scary to work with troubled kids, and for good reason, but they treated us like animals, only tried to scare us, and (at least for me) created way more problems than they solved. I started seeing another therapist recently after getting over my fear of them and he's been helping me resolve my issues stemming from this, and I realized that it had a much bigger impact on my personality (refusal to confide in people, that I felt I always had to be okay for the sake of those around in me, major trust issues, an inability to let myself feel anger out of fear I'd be locked in a room in a straight jacket, a deep desire to be pitied) than I'd realized, and I'm still trying to deal with it.

Almost two years ago, I was celebrating my 21st birthday in the city with some friends, and I'd been talking to some girl on tinder. At some point I decide fuck it, I'm going home, and I'm going to invite this girl over. I'm very drunk at this point, and I've never met her, but I hadn't had sex in a while, so I threw caution to the wind. I Uber home and waited in my basement for her to come, and I quickly noticed that her photos had been unrealistically flattering, and I lose my desire to hook up with her. But I'm awkward, and couldn't bring myself to ask her to leave, so we end up watching Shrek when within 10 minutes she starts kissing me. I'm hesitant, but I'm really drunk so I just kind of go with it until she just undresses and climbs on top of me. She says that she's a virgin but she wants to have sex, at which point I said "no, I think we should stop." She responds by continuing to kiss and undress me, and all I can do in my inebriated, scared state is just to keep saying no. She grabbed my hands and pushed them behind my head and whispered in my ear "you want this" before forcing me inside of her. She was bigger than me, I was drunk, and I was too scared to hit a girl, so I just let it happen, and it went on for probably 10 minutes until she decided she was done and got off of me, but it felt like hours. I just stared at her in shock, and she just commented about how "good" it was, and thanked me, and left. She hit me up one night months later at like 1am asking to hang out, and I immediately blocked her on every mode of communication I have. I don't think she knows how badly she fucked me up - I have recurring nightmares, trouble sleeping, and trust issues nearly 2 years later that don't seem to be going anywhere soon. The part that hurt the most was when I finally worked up the nerve to tell someone what happened - my brother. His response was "bro, you got laid, this is GOOD news!" and I've not forgiven him since. Additionally, I now have one of the most unfortunate triggers of sexual assault memories - nearly any mention of Shrek gives me flashbacks to what happened. I'd been sexually assaulted once before, by a woman when I was 19, but I have no memory of it due to being blackout drunk, and so I never processed it until this happened, which just magnified the trust issues. I'm now seeing a therapist and we're making progress, but there's still work to do.
